AFL tribunal live updates: Brisbane's Lachie Neale challenges striking ban ahead of grand final
Brisbane Lions star Lachie Neale has failed in his attempt to overturn a one-game ban for striking Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan at the AFL tribunal and will miss Saturday's grand final against Fremantle.

Neale's "gut-punch" on Ginnivan means the former Brisbane co-captain has played his last game for the Lions, as the team prepares to face the Fremantle Dockers on Saturday, seeking a second premiership three-peat in club history.
Follow all the proceedings and news in our live blog.

The hearing has ended
The hearing has ended, the screens have all disappeared.
There was no indication from Lachie Neale's counsel, Adrian Anderson, whether there was an intended appeal.

Lachie Neale fails in his appeal and will miss the grand final
We have no problem saying that this was an intentional strike and that it was medium impact.
There is no single frame that shows him contacting Ginnivan.
But Ginnivan doubles over not consistent with being bodychecked.
We place little emphasis on Neale's evidence of Ginnivan's words.
We find this was a forceful blow.
It was to use the vernacular that it was a "strike to the guts".
There is no doubt it should be graded as medium impact.
It is relevant that this took place off the play.
We are mindful of the considerable consequences to Mr Neale.
This brings us to the more difficult issue of whether there are exceptional and compelling circumstances.
It was forcefully put on behalf of Neale that he should not be suspended.
Gleeson says the Tribunal have come to the conclusion that this should not occur.
The purpose of the guidelines are to eliminate this act.
Lachie Neale will remain suspended and will miss the grand final.

Protecting the head a priority for AFL (and all sports)

Should we be more concerned about the incessant gambling, alcohol and fast food sponsors the AFL supports, hits off the ball that result in no penalty or lack of HIA checks when it comes to enrolling our kids in junior football? - This Is Serious Mum

Should we be more concerned about the incessant gambling, alcohol and fast food sponsors the AFL supports, hits off the ball that result in no penalty or lack of HIA checks when it comes to enrolling our kids in junior football?
- This Is Serious Mum
This is Serious Mum,
While this case has serious implications for one player's career, it is not necessarily going to be precedent-setting.
If you ask ME what the biggest concern is, I would say (as the father of a sports-mad kid now pushing adulthood), that the absolute number one issue in AFL is concussion and head protection.

HIA checks are vitally important, and just as important is that they are non-pressurised HIA checks. Whether it is junior footy, club footy, state leagues or AFL, it is crucial that we can depend on the checks being done properly, and that team benefits or potential problems have nothing to do with the outcome.
It's not the result of the game that's important when it comes to safety of players.

Court option no guarantee for Lions
Assuming Neale’s suspension is upheld, which in my view it absolutely should be, can he take it to the high court and run out the clock? - Stephen
Assuming Neale’s suspension is upheld, which in my view it absolutely should be, can he take it to the high court and run out the clock?
- Stephen
Stephen,
IF (I stress if) the Lions lose tonight's case, then they could take the case to the Supreme Court of Victoria, as the Swans did with Andrew Dunkley in 1996.

They wouldn't be trying to run out the clock, rather they would be seeking an injunction against the decision, stating (no doubt) that Neale would not have natural justice regarding another hearing this week.
In the Dunkley case, the injunction was granted, he played the game (and lost) - and then was given a three-match ban the following week.

Is it about the law, or the vibe?

It's not just a GF, and Lachie's last game for the Lions. It's the opportunity to lead and participate in a potential 3rd GF legacy. Lachie is a huge part of why this team has been so successful. Blurred vision and pretty minor incident with no harm done. Let him play! - Winter

It's not just a GF, and Lachie's last game for the Lions. It's the opportunity to lead and participate in a potential 3rd GF legacy. Lachie is a huge part of why this team has been so successful. Blurred vision and pretty minor incident with no harm done. Let him play!

Winter,
In one sense I can't argue with your points. There is a historic "defining moment" in Lachie Neale's career on the line.
However. He didn't have to run towards Ginnivan (and away from the ball). He didn't have to make contact - he could have yelled something pithy on his way by.

He didn't have to knock him over. I don't see why a leader / veteran of a team in the second-most consequential game of the season (trying to get to the most consequential game of the season) would bring on an incident like this?
It's not a fantastic outcome either way, IMHO.

It's not quite that simple here
Answer the question about the weather, but not: What is the difference between medium and low impact???? - Mark
Answer the question about the weather, but not: What is the difference between medium and low impact????
- Mark
Mark,
Low impact is for low force or minimal contact where the player gets up quickly.
Medium impact is for greater force OR off-the-ball incidents.

So Neale's team is arguing it's minimal force, and Ginnivan wasn't injured and got up straight away. The AFL is arguing that it was enough to knock him over, and the potential to injure is there AND it's off-the-ball.
